## CEO overview

- **What is changing:** Firstmate stops asking the captain about paused work whose worker has already gone away and whose task is finished or frozen at a captain gate. It keeps asking when a worker is still present, when an outside dependency is genuinely pending, when another mate is holding a decision, and when work may actually be stuck.
- **Why it matters:** The last message on a finished task often still reads "paused". Supervision took that at face value forever, so it woke the captain about the same dead lane every hour with nobody left who could answer.
- **Customer or business impact:** The captain gets fewer meaningless supervision alerts during normal work and during walk-away periods, while real waits, held decisions, and genuinely stuck work stay just as visible as before.
- **Risk and rollout:** Low. Silence applies only to ordinary work that is both proven finished or captain-frozen and proven to have no live worker, and that conclusion expires and is re-checked rather than being permanent. Anything failed, resumed, live, uncertain, or belonging to another mate keeps its existing alert path. This change ships behind no feature flag because it only narrows which alerts are raised; rolling it back is a single revert.

## What changed technically

- Added one shared declared-wait classification that combines the authoritative crew state, the task kind, and backend agent liveness, and is used by both normal and away-mode supervision so the two modes cannot disagree.
- Settled stale `paused:` and verified `captain-held` declarations only for dead ordinary workers on completed or parked lanes, under a classification that expires and revalidates state and liveness.
- Routed unchanged and changing pane hashes through the same marker-aware watcher handling, so live and uncertain waits surface once, genuine waits keep their bounded cadence, resumed work keeps wedge aging, and an invalidated settlement surfaces immediately.
- Kept every secondmate declaration on its bounded recheck cadence without reading remote secondmate state or endpoint liveness, so remote transport cannot block away-mode housekeeping.
- Limited away-mode reclassification to the stale due boundary once stale tracking owns a lane, preserving bounded housekeeping and wedge detection for working or failed lanes whose status log still ends in `paused:`.
- Added executable watcher and daemon regressions for changing-hash re-arms, settlement expiry, live and uncertain waits, secondmate holds, resumed and failed work, and persistent wedges.
- Refreshed the portable serial shard duration hints in `bin/fm-test-run.sh` from the latest green timing artifacts. The previous hints were three weeks stale, so shard 3 carried about 17m36s of real work against a 10m57s estimate and hit the 20 minute job cap on this branch and on `main`. The refreshed hints rebalance the four shards to about 13.8 minutes each.
- Updated the supervision architecture, configuration reference, Herdr integration note, away-mode skill, and the portable shard document to match the shipped behaviour.

## Validation

- **Checks passed:** The four suites that own this change all pass locally against this branch: watcher triage, away-mode daemon, crew state, and inactive reconcile. The pull request communication suite passes 15 of 15, the documentation ownership check passes, the full repository lint passes, and the shard coverage guard reports a complete and disjoint partition of 167 scripts. Every hosted product check passes on this branch: both behaviour parallel shards, all four behaviour serial shards, the Herdr lane, the stock macOS snapshot lane, the timing aggregate, the coverage guard, lint, and the repository invariants. The latest hosted run also confirms the shard rebalance: the four serial shards finished between about eleven and fifteen minutes against the twenty minute cap, where before the rebalance the two slowest ran out of time and were cancelled.
- **Checks not run:** The two hosted communication checks have not passed on any head, because they read the live pull request description and that description still carries the pipeline-generated legacy headings; replacing it with this narrative, and the hosted verification that follows, remain for the outer executor. No visual check applies: this is a headless supervision daemon with no rendered surface.
- **Evidence and limitations:** The two new watcher regressions were run against the pre-change code and fail there, and pass on this branch. Beyond unit assertions, the real watcher was driven against a real terminal window whose worker had exited, for six supervision rounds under the reported condition of a changing pane hash and an aged long cadence, and the real wake drain output was read as the captain would receive it. The pre-change code delivers six actionable alerts on a dead finished lane and six on a dead parked gate; this branch delivers none and records them as absorbed. In the same harness a live worker on a genuine external wait and a captain-held transfer still produce their six bounded rechecks with their exact wording, and a stuck worker with no declared wait still arms its wedge timer, so nothing was weakened. The limitation is that those fixtures prove routing and marker behaviour without a live production fleet, so final hosted execution and captain review remain the rollout gates.

## Module-boundary decision

Current modules retained. The shared state-and-liveness decision belongs in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh`, the normal watcher's marker transitions belong in `bin/fm-watch.sh`, and away-mode tracking belongs in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh`. That keeps a single classification contract without creating another supervisor or duplicating backend policy.

## Decision needed

No product decision required. The captain retains merge authority and this pull request is not to be merged automatically.
